name: Creativity Guru session plan
description: The real plan, transcribed from "IDEM104 - Session Plan Creativity Guru Case (Case 2).md" — built across several rounds, a live rehearsal and a mentor meeting. Total 145 min plus the untimed introduction (target 150, matching Xemia; Problem Finding was trimmed by 5 after mentor feedback that it ran long). One structural note: this document's own math puts the ice breaker inside Problem Finding's 45-minute budget, not in a separate Introduction block — the app's Introduction section is left empty here to match that, even though the base framework lists Introduction as its own section.
problemOwnerDescription: Course coordinator for IDEM104, representing the course's other owners. Received the creativity legacy — roughly 100 books and a CF suitcase of random objects — from Mark, who lectured the course for about 25 years before his death two weeks before this session. Gave no written brief; stated the problem live and asked the team to draft one or two problem statements themselves. Wants something tangible to hand over to students afterward (a poster or a booklet), and said he can personally make a bold, low-scoring idea work himself — protect at least one audacious option rather than scoring it out. Source: IDEM104 - MoM Case 2 Check-in with Sem Carree; IDEM104 - Session Plan Creativity Guru Case (Case 2).md.
problemAsGiven:
Sem and the course owners hold a legacy of creativity knowledge and materials: books, techniques, mindsets, slide decks and objects. They do not want to lose it.

The gap: a shelf of books or a library exists, but the value for students lies in use, inspiration and a stretched mindset. Passing on a book alone does not make students use it — two routes exist, knowledge and physical items, and each needs its own answer.

As given by Sem: How to make the knowledge and materials of creativity gurus benefit students, so students use them, get inspired and stretch their mindset?
introduction:
Sem presents the case as problem owner. The team facilitates. Sem owns the content, the team owns the process.

Case background: client is Sem Carree and the course owners, TU Delft Creative Facilitation course. Target user: design students at TU Delft (programme, year and prior creativity training to confirm with Sem). The legacy of the gurus does not reach students in a form they use. A long-time lecturer of the course died two weeks ago and left his books and objects to Sem; Sem decides how to tell this.

What is the legacy: gurus Osborn, Koestler, Runco and De Bono, each with a different style, some close by at TU Delft. Materials: about 100 creativity books, a CF suitcase of random objects, slide decks and mindsets. Two routes: get the knowledge to students, and make the physical items benefit students.

Source: IDEM104 - Session Plan Creativity Guru Case (Case 2).md.
